subject: humanities
passage: Published in 1958, Chinua Achebe's ______ Fall Apart follows Okonkwo, a proud and ambitious man in a fictional Igbo village, through the years in which British missionaries and colonial officials first arrive in the region that is now southeastern Nigeria. Its title comes from a line in W. B. Yeats's poem "The Second Coming," which imagines a world in which established order collapses, an image that Achebe's story places in a specific historical setting.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: Achebe wrote several novels, so the title Things Fall Apart is essential: it tells which of his novels the sentence means. Essential information is not set off by punctuation. The sentence also offers no closing mark after the title, so any opening comma, colon, or dash would be left without a partner.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The title is essential, so it shouldn't be set off; in addition, a single comma here would separate the subject from its verb "follows" with no matching comma after the title.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A colon must follow a complete independent clause, but "Published in 1958, Chinua Achebe's novel" is not one.
explanation.C: Correct. No punctuation is used because the title is essential information identifying which of Achebe's novels is meant.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A dash would begin a pair of dashes around nonessential information, but the title is essential and no closing dash follows.
